topic: timing race — same clock function called twice across an assertion boundary
question: Quick reminder — what was the actual root cause?
butterfly_answer: Two independent `time.Now()` calls — one in `NewToken` when the token was created, one in `IsExpired()` when checked. CI jitter between those two calls caused the token to appear expired before it should have been.
lastN_answer: The prior context doesn't mention a root cause — the conversation is entirely about code style and consistency topics (error messages, var/const, eslint, error handling, test organization). No bug or incident root cause was discussed.
needle_fact: The flake is caused by two independent `time.Now()` calls straddling the assertion — one inside `NewToken` setting `createdAt`, and a second inside `IsExpired()` — with no shared timestamp, so scheduler jitter between the two reads can exceed the 50ms safety margin and push `IsExpired()` past the TTL boundary.
